description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is transaction.TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and the transaction inventory row '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |', which sits at README.md:224 in this checkout - the Agent Action Plan cites :222 for that same row and :224 is the line the file actually holds, so the verified number is used and the discrepancy is stated rather than propagated (practice B1). Both readings are the inverse of the prompt's mapping and the mirror image of parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. Rule R1 governs the resolution - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure: the divergence is documented here and never silently corrected, and the Agent Action Plan escalates it for explicit user confirmation. Nothing is downgraded to read-only to match the name: this case rejects an add rather than declining to attempt one, and the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is pinned at its full 350 bytes by case19 and case20. GATE G12 - CSUTLDTC IS A SPRING @Service AND NEVER A JOB: app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl carries no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl, app/proc or app/csd, so it is a called subprogram rather than a batch step, invoked exactly four times - twice by CORPT00C at :392 and :412 and twice by COTRN02C at :393 and :413. Its prompt-mandated Java name is util.DateUtilityJob and rule R1 keeps that name verbatim, while implicit requirement I3 fixes the shape: the class is annotated @Service, is never a Spring Batch Job, Step or Tasklet, is constructor-injected into transaction.TransactionViewController and is called as a plain Java method. This case reaches it that way and no other - unit kind CONTROLLER_POJO, the controller built through its constructor and its MAIN-PARA method called directly, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no JobLauncher between the assertion and the decision (gate G51). WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES - THE THIRD BRANCH OF A TWO-LEVEL NESTED IF: the acceptance rule at the first call site (:397-407) is not one test but two, nested, and all three of its outcomes have to be read separately, because the rule's exact shape is preserved rather than simplified (practice B5). (1) severity = '0000' - the outer IF is true and CONTINUE accepts outright; case15 drives it with 2022-07-18 at both sites. (2) severity is not '0000' AND message number = '2513' - the outer IF is false, the inner IF at :400 is false as well, so nothing whatever happens and the error is TOLERATED; case16 drives it with 1500-01-01, a date before the Lillian epoch CEEDAYS supports. (3) severity is not '0000' AND message number is not '2513' - the inner IF is true and :401-405 reject. THIS CASE IS (3). Collapsing the nesting into 'severity = 0000 OR message = 2513' would reach the same verdict here and would still misdescribe the program: the two spans are read independently, at their own offsets, out of one 80-byte area, and it is precisely because 2513 WOULD have been tolerated that this rejection is evidence of anything at all. THE TOKEN, DECODED FROM THE 88-LEVEL HEX RATHER THAN ASSUMED (practice B1): TORIGDTI is 2022-13-01. app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:60-70 declares each CEEDAYS feedback token as an eight-byte hex VALUE over FEEDBACK-TOKEN-VALUE, whose first halfword is SEVERITY PIC S9(4) BINARY and whose second is MSG-NO PIC S9(4) BINARY, followed by CASE-SEV-CTL PIC X and a three-byte FACILITY-ID - 2 + 2 + 1 + 3 = 8 bytes. The token this date produces is FC-INVALID-MONTH, declared at :67 as X'000309D559C3C5C5': X'0003' is severity 3, X'09D5' is 9*256 + 213 = decimal 2517, X'59' is the severity-control byte and X'C3C5C5' is EBCDIC 'CEE'. Its fifteen-character WS-RESULT text is 'Invalid month  ' - thirteen characters padded to the declared X(15) - and month 13 pairs with it exactly: 13 is a month value no calendar has, which is what FC-INVALID-MONTH names, and it is the one kind of input that is positionally flawless and semantically impossible at the same time. The complete nine-token table, every severity and message number decoded the same arithmetic way and every result text taken from the ordered EVALUATE at :128-149 whose WHEN OTHER is last (gate G30), is: FC-INVALID-DATE X'0000000000000000' severity 0 message 0 'Date is valid'; FC-INSUFFICIENT-DATA X'000309CB59C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2507 'Insufficient'; FC-BAD-DATE-VALUE X'000309CC59C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2508 'Datevalue error'; FC-INVALID-ERA X'000309CD59C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2509 'Invalid Era    '; FC-UNSUPP-RANGE X'000309D159C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2513 'Unsupp. Range  '; FC-INVALID-MONTH X'000309D559C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2517 'Invalid month  '; FC-BAD-PIC-STRING X'000309D659C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2518 'Bad Pic String '; FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA X'000309D859C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2520 'Nonnumeric data'; FC-YEAR-IN-ERA-ZERO X'000309D959C3C5C5' severity 3 message 2521 'YearInEra is 0 '; and the unmatched WHEN OTHER arm 'Date is invalid'. X'09CB' is 2507, X'09D1' is 2513 and X'09D5' is 2517, each converted here rather than carried over. THE 80-BYTE CSUTLDTC-RESULT, SUMMED TWICE (practice B11). COTRN02C declares its own view of the returned area at :62-69: CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD PIC X(04) at bytes 1-4, FILLER PIC X(11) at 5-15, CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM PIC X(04) at 16-19 and CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG PIC X(61) at 20-80, so 4 + 11 + 4 + 61 = 80. That view aligns byte for byte with CSUTLDTC's own WS-MESSAGE at :42-57, which is WS-SEVERITY PIC X(04) at 1-4 with WS-SEVERITY-N REDEFINES it as PIC 9(4), FILLER PIC X(11) VALUE 'Mesg Code:' at 5-15, WS-MSG-NO PIC X(04) at 16-19 with WS-MSG-NO-N REDEFINES it as PIC 9(4), FILLER PIC X(01) at 20, WS-RESULT PIC X(15) at 21-35, FILLER PIC X(01) at 36, FILLER PIC X(09) VALUE 'TstDate:' at 37-45, WS-DATE PIC X(10) at 46-55, FILLER PIC X(01) at 56, FILLER PIC X(10) VALUE 'Mask used:' at 57-66, WS-DATE-FMT PIC X(10) at 67-76, FILLER PIC X(01) at 77 and FILLER PIC X(03) at 78-80, so 4 + 11 + 4 + 1 + 15 + 1 + 9 + 10 + 1 + 10 + 10 + 1 + 3 = 80 as well. The image this date returns is stated in full rather than left vague (practice B8): '0003', then 'Mesg Code: ', then '2517', then one space, then 'Invalid month  ', then one space, then 'TstDate: ', then the ten bytes X'000A' followed by '2022-13-', then one space, then 'Mask used:', then 'YYYY-MM-DD', then one space, then three spaces. COTRN02C READS ONLY BYTES 1-4 AND 16-19; the remaining 61 bytes are opaque to it, so they are recorded here for the reader and are not asserted, the model carrying no member for a called subprogram's internal area. Two source facts account for the odd bytes 46-55, and both are preserved rather than repaired (practice B5): INITIALIZE WS-MESSAGE at :90 does not clear FILLER items, so the three literals survive into every returned image; and :122 MOVE WS-DATE-TO-TEST TO WS-DATE is a GROUP move over a two-byte S9(4) BINARY length prefix, so WS-DATE receives the big-endian halfword X'000A' - Vstring-length 10, always 10 because LENGTH OF LS-DATE returns the declared width - and then only the FIRST EIGHT date characters, overwriting the clean copy :107-108 had already placed there. The definitive treatment of that quirk belongs to parity/CSUTLDTC, which owns CSUTLDTC's own twenty cases; it is noted here because it is real, and it is not asserted here because COTRN02C never looks at it. THE SUBPROGRAM'S RETURN CODE DOES NOT PROPAGATE, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE POINT: CSUTLDTC.cbl:98 MOVE WS-SEVERITY-N TO RETURN-CODE makes CSUTLDTC's own return code 3 for this token - 0 for a valid date and 3 for every one of the eight named errors - and util.DateUtilityJob reports that 3 on its result. COTRN02C never reads it. The program contains ZERO CALL 'CEE3ABD', counted across all 783 lines, sets no RETURN-CODE of its own, and ends this path with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID rather than an abend. expectedReturnCode here is therefore 0, explicitly not 3. Gate G35 is deliberately NOT asserted for that reason, and neither are G32 (zero GO TO in this program, so there is no backward jump to restructure), G39 (no pagination on this screen) or G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC). Gate G36 - the exact 80-byte composition and the nine result strings as behaviour under test - belongs to parity/CSUTLDTC; what is under test here is the acceptance RULE. THE SIBLING CALL SITE, DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN GIVEN A FILE OF ITS OWN: gate G15 fixes this folder at exactly twenty cases, so the second call site is described here and driven by a sibling. :409-427 repeats the first site against TPROCDTI verbatim - the same MOVE of WS-DATE-FORMAT into CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT, the same MOVE SPACES TO CSUTLDTC-RESULT, the same CALL, and the same two-level nested acceptance rule with the same '2513' tolerance - and differs in exactly two observable ways: the literal it moves to WS-MESSAGE is 'Proc Date - Not a valid date...' rather than 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...', and the -1 goes to TPROCDTL rather than TORIGDTL. A translation that shared either the literal or the cursor field between the two sites would pass this case and fail its sibling. In this folder case18 drives that second site's rejection, with FC-BAD-DATE-VALUE - X'000309CC59C3C5C5', severity 3, message 2508, 'Datevalue error' - from 2022-02-30, a day that month does not have; and case16 drives the '2513' tolerance. Naming which sibling actually holds which branch, rather than restating an allocation from the authoring brief, is practice B12. TWO SEPARATE LAYERS, AND THIS DATE PASSES THE FIRST IN ORDER TO REACH THE SECOND: the positional guard at :353-366 is an EVALUATE TRUE over five reference-modified spans - TORIGDTI(1:4) numeric, (5:1) equal '-', (6:2) numeric, (8:1) equal '-', (9:2) numeric - which decomposes the X(10) field as 4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10, and whose failure emits a different literal, 'Orig Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD', with its own -1 to TORIGDTL. 2022-13-01 satisfies every one of those five tests, so that EVALUATE takes WHEN OTHER and CONTINUEs, and it is the semantic CSUTLDTC check at :389-407 that rejects it. case14 drives the positional layer instead, with '2022/07/18', whose (5:1) is not '-'. Holding the two apart matters because a translation that folded the semantic check into the positional one would emit the wrong message text, put the same message on both failures, and make the two layers indistinguishable from the outside. WHAT RAN BEFORE THE REJECTION, AND IS THEREFORE ASSERTED: the key fields resolve first. ACTIDINI holds eleven digits, so the class test at :197 passes; FUNCTION NUMVAL at :204 converts them; :206-207 move the result into XREF-ACCT-ID and back into ACTIDINI; READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :576-585 answers DFHRESP (NORMAL) from the one seeded base cluster (gates G47 and G45); and :209 moves XREF-CARD-NUM into CARDNINI, which is where the sixteen-digit card number in this case's echo comes from. All eleven blank-field arms, the two numeric arms on TTYPCDI and TCATCDI, the positional amount guard at :339-351 and both positional date guards then fall through. :383-386 re-edits the amount BEFORE either date is validated: COMPUTE WS-TRAN-AMT-N = FUNCTION NUMVAL-C(TRNAMTI), MOVE WS-TRAN-AMT-N TO WS-TRAN-AMT-E PIC +99999999.99, MOVE WS-TRAN-AMT-E TO TRNAMTI. TRNAMTO is consequently asserted in its RE-EDITED +99999999.99 form, '+00000012.34' at the field's declared X(12) width, and the conversion runs through common.CobolDecimal at scale 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN - never HALF_UP, never HALF_EVEN, never a double or a float - because ROUNDED appears zero times in all twenty-eight programs (rules R2, R3 and R4, gates G23 and G24). For this value the edit is idempotent, which is said plainly rather than glossed: '+00000012.34' already matches the mask, so what the expectation pins is the mask's shape and the fact that the step ran, not a change of digits. WHAT IS NOT REACHED, ASSERTED AS THE NON-EVENT IT IS: SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN at :516-534 performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :518, moves WS-MESSAGE to ERRMSGO at :520, sends the map at :522-528 and then ends with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :530-534, so it is TERMINAL: the CICS task ends inside it and control never returns to the statement after the PERFORM at :405. The second CSUTLDTC call at :413 therefore never happens, the merchant-id guard at :430 never runs, and ADD-TRANSACTION with its backward browse at :644-706 and its EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is never entered. TPROCDTI is a fully valid 2022-07-18 precisely so that its validity cannot be what stops the run; the run stops before that date is looked at, and exactly one screen is sent. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion that nothing was written, and TRANSACT's final state is the pre-state row for row - three rows, byte-identical to the seed, at exactly 350 bytes each - with row 0 additionally pinned across all fourteen CVTRA05Y spans by their verbatim copybook names, the trailing FILLER PIC X(20) among them, which is what proves the FILLER was emitted at all (gates G19 and G21). TRAN-AMT is pinned as its stored eleven-byte image '0000000010A' rather than as a quantity, because the gate is byte parity and the zoned sign overpunch that makes it +1.01 is part of the value. No control transfers anywhere, so there is no EXEC CICS XCTL on this path and gate G40 has no subject here: the termination is RETURN_TRANSID and the response names this same screen as its next target, which is what makes the payload a legal next request. ONE MESSAGE, TWO DECLARED WIDTHS: :401-402 moves exactly one literal - 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...', spaced hyphen, trailing ellipsis, thirty-one characters - into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80), and :520 then moves that 80-byte field into ERRMSGO PIC X(78). The receiver is two bytes narrower, so COBOL loses the last two bytes on the right (rule R5), and the two widths are two distinct observations rather than one repeated: expectedMessages carries the single message text on channel WS_MESSAGE_80 space-padded to 80 and on channel SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 space-padded to 78, the latter being the value ERRMSGO carries on the send. Declaring only one of the two would make the two-byte loss unobservable. ERRMSGC is pinned at its default DFHDFCOL rather than DFHGREEN, because :727 assigns DFHGREEN on the successful-write arm and nowhere else, so a rejecting path leaves the colour byte as it found it; the mnemonic comes from common.BmsAttributes, which reproduces the absent DFHBMSCA from IBM CICS documentation (risk R-D). The error flag is on and the cursor is on TORIGDTL, which is how the REENTER half of gate G38 is discharged: CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as '1', so :120 finds CDEMO-PGM-REENTER true, the map is received and revalidated rather than painted fresh, and the -1 that positions the cursor is the only -1 in this run. TORIGDTL is an xxxL length item and therefore validation metadata, never a JSON payload member; it appears as cursorField, which is the model's name for the length item that received MOVE -1. No other xxxL is -1. THE TWO DATASETS THIS CASE SEEDS, AND THE TWO IT DOES NOT. CCXREF is seeded from five rows of cardxref.txt exactly as they ship, 36 bytes wide, and is deliberately NOT pre-padded: app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares CARD-XREF-RECORD as XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) + XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) + XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) + FILLER X(14) = 50 and the fixture omits that trailing FILLER, so the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below supplies the fourteen spaces once, at seed time, before anything decodes a row, and it is the sole owner of that repair (gate G16, risk R-F). Row 0 of the fixture is '0500024453765740' then '000000050' then '00000000050', so the ACTIDIN this case sends is the account key occupying record bytes 26-36 and the card number it resolves to is the key at bytes 1-16. TRANSACT is seeded with three 350-byte rows inline because no ASCII fixture ships for that master - it is populated online rather than loaded - each summed span by span from app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy as 16 + 2 + 4 + 10 + 100 + 11 + 9 + 50 + 50 + 10 + 16 + 26 + 26 + 20 = 350. CXACAIX is NOT seeded as a dataset of its own: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:63-65 defines it as 'ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY' with an AIX.PATH DSNAME over the CCXREF base, so the read at :578 resolves through the one seeded base cluster as an alternate-index finder and never through a second table (gate G45). AND ACCTDAT IS NOT SEEDED EITHER, BECAUSE IT IS A DEAD DECLARATION (practice B5): WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' is declared at :40 and COPY CVACT01Y at :89, and neither is referenced anywhere in the program - every DATASET operand names CXACAIX at :579, CCXREF at :612, or TRANSACT at :645, :676, :705 and :714, and no field of the 300-byte ACCOUNT-RECORD is ever moved. ParityHarness.seed states that inputs names every dataset the unit under test will read, so seeding the account master would assert a read that does not exist; there is accordingly no ACCTDAT entry in inputs, in expectedWrites, in expectedFinalState or in expectedDatasets, here or in any of the nineteen sibling cases, and the deadness is preserved rather than tidied away or helpfully completed. Were it ever read it would bind to fixtures/acctdata.txt at fifty 300-byte rows, and that binding is recorded here so the omission reads as a decision rather than an oversight. Every dataset is addressed by its application.yml binding key rather than by name, so not one fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file (gate G46); no tenth fixture is named, the set being closed at the nine derived from app/data/ASCII; and the code page is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). STATELESSNESS AND THE 218-BYTE AREA (rule R6, gate G37): EIBCALEN is 218, which is app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy's 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA - 4 + 8 + 4 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 25 + 25 + 11 + 1 + 16 + 7 + 7 = 160 - plus the 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension COTRN02C appends at :72-80, which is 16 + 16 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 16 = 58. The extension stays a separate DTO member and is never folded into the shared common.NavigationContext, because it belongs to this program alone. All twenty-two fields of the area are pinned on the response and none is omitted: the conversation state - the commarea, the attention identifier and the screen's own field values - travels in the request and response payloads and never in server-side session state, so an unpinned field is a field nobody has checked. The AID is DFHENTER, resolved through common.CicsAid; DFHAID itself is IBM-supplied and absent from this repository, so its mnemonics are reproduced from IBM CICS documentation (risk R-D). The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the single instant all twenty cases in this folder use, and both date inputs are fixed literals rather than anything derived from today, so POPULATE-HEADER-INFO's CURDATEO '07/19/22' and CURTIMEO '23:12:34' are comparable byte for byte and the run is deterministic in any timezone (practice B7). The three free-text received items are declared as the operator's keystrokes and reach their declared X(60), X(30) and X(25) widths through the PIC X move, which is why the echo is asserted at full width. BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS, SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO in app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl and of A000-MAIN in app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl, with every token severity and message number DECODED FROM THE 88-LEVEL HEX VALUES at CSUTLDTC.cbl:60-70 rather than assumed, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts (CVTRA05Y 350, CVACT03Y 50, COCOM01Y 160, and CVACT01Y 300 whose misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE would be preserved verbatim by any case that pinned it), against the twenty-one xxxI and xxxO widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY whose group image sums to 12 + 21*7 + 396 = 555 with ERRMSG at X(78), and against the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt. It was NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL. Running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment and Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 establishes that with eight independently verified blockers; the one that bites hardest here is that cobc --list-intrinsics matches ZERO CEE* entries, so the CEEDAYS service CSUTLDTC calls at :116-120 cannot be invoked at all, and there is no CICS emulator and no DFHAID or DFHBMSCA in the repository either. The change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. TWO POINTS OF THE AUTHORING BRIEF RECONCILED IN THE OPEN (practice B4). First, the brief asks for the injected util.DateUtilityJob outcome to be DECLARED. ParityCase - the frozen wire contract, which wins on any disagreement - models no member for a called subprogram's returned area, and COTRN02CParityTest deliberately wires a REAL DateUtilityJob rather than a stub, on the stated ground that the service is deterministic and that stubbing it would assert the controller against a fiction. The outcome is therefore declared where the contract allows it to be: this case supplies the date, and the severity '0003', the message number '2517', the fifteen-character result 'Invalid month  ' and the complete eighty-byte image the deterministic service returns for it are all set out above, offset by offset. Second, the brief asks for exactly one expectedMessages entry. The harness reports WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO as two separate channels whenever a screen is sent, because :520 loses two bytes between them, so a single entry would leave the diff count non-zero and fail gate G18 while asserting strictly less. What is honoured is the substance: ONE message text, projected onto its two declared widths. Neither reconciliation weakens an expectation, invents a member or renames anything. NO USER RULES EXIST: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the whole document, so no user rule forces this file into scope and no user rule constrains how it is written. Per UR4 the absence is stated explicitly and is not treated as permission to lower the bar; the standard held here is the Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 enterprise practices, cited by name where they bite - B1 (every literal derived and verified and every hex conversion computed, and nothing left unresolved anywhere), B3 (the reference trees app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd and app/data are read-only and were read, never edited), B4 (the R-B inversion and both brief reconciliations disclosed), B5 (the acceptance rule's exact shape preserved, including that message 2513 WOULD have been tolerated, and the ACCTDAT declaration and CVACT01Y include left dead), B7 (a pinned clock and pinned date literals, nothing computed from today), B8 (an explicit token decode, the full eighty-byte image, the exact message text, the named -1 target, binding keys rather than dataset names and a named code page), B11 (eighty summed twice, the date field decomposed as 4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10, the group image 555 and the commarea 160 + 58 = 218) and B12 (the provenance statement and the sibling allocation stated as they actually are). Rules R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 are all in force and are cited above where each bites, R7 being satisfied by the preserved EVALUATE order with WHEN OTHER last and by the fact that this program contains no GO TO to restructure. GATES DISCHARGED HERE: G12, G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G23, G24, G30, G37, G38, G45, G46, G47 and G51. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, because this program has no subject for them: G32, G35, G36, G39, G40 and G43.
